title: LLMs from scratch and research methods
summary: Model-side depth for research/ML engineers: reproduce GPT-2 124M with build-nanogpt, then the CS336 (Spring 2026) summit at reduced scale — A1 basics, data filtering/dedup, FLOPs/memory accounting and scaling laws, base-model evaluation, GQA/MLA/MoE, SSM/hybrid awareness, optional nanochat end to end — plus research methods (paper reading, pre-registered experiments, reproduction reports). Prerequisites are M08 + M09 (not M13); every compute-heavy step has a free-GPU/CPU scale-down. Optional for the three job tracks.

practice.title: Reduced-scale GPT-2 reproduction
practice.brief: Reproduce build-nanogpt at reduced scale (10–50M params on a FineWeb-Edu sample on a free T4/Kaggle GPU). Include mixed precision (fp16+GradScaler on T4, bf16 where supported), gradient accumulation, torch.compile if available, and a val-loss + HellaSwag-style eval hook. Kill the run mid-way, resume, and show the loss continues identically (same data position and RNG).
practice.done_when: A loss plot spanning a kill/resume boundary with no jump, tokens/sec before/after each speed-up, and an eval-hook log.

quiz.prompt: Gradient accumulation lets you:
options: Simulate a larger batch size with limited GPU memory
quiz.explain: Sum gradients over micro-batches (scaled), then step once.

quiz.prompt: bf16 mixed precision is preferred over fp16 on modern GPUs mainly because:
options: It uses less memory than fp16
Its wider exponent range avoids most loss-scaling issues
quiz.explain: bf16 keeps fp32's exponent range; fp16 needs a GradScaler (and T4s lack bf16 tensor cores).

quiz.prompt: A correct resume must restore:
options: Weights, optimizer state, LR-scheduler step, data-loader position and RNG state
quiz.explain: Missing any of these changes the trajectory.

quiz.prompt: Your resumed run's loss jumps up for 200 steps. List two likely causes.
rubric: Optimizer state (Adam moments) not restored → effectively a cold optimizer
LR schedule restarted (warmup again / wrong step) or data loader restarted at shard 0
Mentions RNG/dropout or mixed-precision scaler state as secondary causes

quiz.prompt: AdamW differs from Adam + L2 regularization by:
options: Decoupling weight decay from the gradient-based update
quiz.explain: Loshchilov & Hutter: decay is applied directly to weights, not through the adaptive gradient.

quiz.prompt: Regex pre-tokenization before BPE mainly prevents:
options: Merges across word/category boundaries such as letters with punctuation
quiz.explain: It stops tokens like 'dog.' or 'dog!' from becoming separate merged units.

quiz.prompt: With warmup + cosine decay, the LR at the final step is:
quiz.explain: Cosine anneals from max to min_lr over the decay horizon.

quiz.prompt: MinHash + LSH is used for:
quiz.explain: It estimates Jaccard similarity without comparing all pairs.

quiz.prompt: A data mixture specifies:
options: The sampling proportions of different sources/domains

quiz.prompt: Benchmark contamination in pretraining data inflates:

quiz.explain: The model has seen test items.

quiz.prompt: Why can aggressive quality filtering hurt low-resource languages like Urdu?
rubric: Quality classifiers/heuristics are trained on English-like 'good' text and misjudge Urdu/Roman-Urdu
Language-ID errors on code-mixed text drop valid documents
Result: tiny remaining Urdu share → worse Urdu capability; mitigation: per-language thresholds

practice.brief: Train 5 tiny models across ~2 orders of magnitude of compute (vary N and D), log FLOPs using 6·N·D, fit a power law of loss vs compute in log-log space, and predict the loss of a 6th run before training it. practice.brief: Evaluate your U01/U02 models and GPT-2 124M on 3 tasks via lm-eval-harness. quiz.prompt: Log-likelihood multiple-choice scoring compares:
options: The model's probability of each answer option
quiz.explain: The option with highest (possibly length-normalized) log-prob is the prediction.

quiz.prompt: A large score change from prompt formatting alone indicates:
options: A measurement sensitivity you must report
quiz.explain: Report the format and compare like with like.

quiz.prompt: Benchmark saturation means:

quiz.explain: Then remaining errors may be label noise.

quiz.prompt: In a top-2 MoE layer, each token is processed by:
options: The 2 experts chosen by the router
quiz.explain: Outputs are combined by the router weights.

quiz.prompt: An MoE load-balancing loss prevents:
options: The router collapsing onto a few experts
quiz.explain: Without it, popular experts get more traffic and more training (rich-get-richer).

quiz.prompt: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) mainly reduces:
options: KV-cache memory by compressing keys/values into a latent
quiz.explain: DeepSeek-V2 caches a low-rank latent instead of full K/V.

quiz.prompt: Why do MoE models have high total parameters but lower per-token compute, and what does that do to serving memory?
rubric: Only k of E experts run per token, so FLOPs scale with active params
All experts must still be held in memory (or sharded), so memory scales with total params
Serving needs expert parallelism / more GPUs despite low FLOPs

quiz.prompt: SSMs like Mamba scale with sequence length roughly:
quiz.explain: A recurrent scan processes each token once with a fixed-size state.

quiz.prompt: A hybrid architecture interleaves:

quiz.prompt: Test-time compute scaling improves answers by:

quiz.prompt: Why haven't SSM-only models displaced Transformers in practice?

capstone.title: Reduced-scale reproduction

levels: Excellent: exact claim quoted; pre-registered hypothesis; justified reduced scale
Excellent: own code passing CS336-style tests; config-driven; resumable
Excellent: ≥3 seeds, confidence intervals, compute log (GPU-hours, cost), plots
Excellent: deviations and negative results explicit; threats to validity
Excellent: 4-page report + public repo + 5-min video walkthrough
